dedupe_keys.name: repurposing natural gas pipelines for hydrogen limits and options for the german nel pipeline

description: This study by Kornel Telessy, Lukas Barner and Franziska Holz of the German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin), TU Berlin and the Norwegian University of Science and Technology, published in the International Journal of Hydrogen Energy in 2024, investigates the challenges and options for repurposing existing natural gas pipelines to carry hydrogen. Coverage: safety challenges from hydrogen embrittlement of pipeline steels and the smaller molecular size of the gas, and the economic challenge of hydrogen's lower volumetric energy density; three options examined in depth are no modification with enhanced maintenance, gaseous inhibitors, and the pipe-in-pipe approach, compared by levelised cost of transport for the German Norddeutsche Erdgasleitung (NEL) pipeline. The options fall in a similar cost range. Format and access: an open journal article. Licence and cost: free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: one pipeline, and the abstract was the part read; the authors expect sunk costs, public acceptance and consumer requirements to shape decisions more than cost. The option costs can parameterise retrofit choices in gas and hydrogen network capacity planning models. It relates to SciGRID_gas and the GreenHyDe German gas-to-hydrogen transition study in the catalogue.
